$comment: Explicit, versioned opt-outs for scripts/breaking_schema_check.py (an ENFORCE, blocking gate). The gate's rule is not 'you may not break the contract' — it is 'you may not break it silently'. A change stays allowed; the silence does not. An entry only grants an opt-out when file, rule, reason, and version are all present, AND reason is real prose explaining WHY the tightening is intentional and reviewed — a bare issue/PR reference, 'TODO', 'see PR', or anything under ~20 chars / a single word is rejected (see reason_rejection()). pointer_prefix is optional and defaults to matching every finding for that rule in that file; add it to scope a narrower, single-field opt-out instead. Entries do not expire — a bound-hardening acknowledgement is a permanent historical fact about that contract, not a lease.

Because the branch count changed, the checker no longer compares branches positionally; the E5 request and 201 changes inside them (requirement and DeclaredTarget becoming typed unions of the unchanged latency shape and the new closed accuracy shape) are still individually acknowledged through agent_readiness_endpoints.json's oneOf_added / additionalProperties / required entries. Latency requests and latency 201 bodies are unchanged.

Private follow-up filed in TraigentBackend as a GitHub issue (linked in the PR description) in case per-resource grants at key-creation time are still wanted later.

dataset_label is a new optional, nullable member on ExperimentGroupOverview added to let the portal's agent+dataset history table show a human-readable dataset name (Benchmark.label) instead of an opaque canonical dataset_id or 'No dataset'. This is the bare-named-resource conservative heuristic: ExperimentGroupOverview is reused response-side only (GET /api/v1/experiment-groups and .../{group_id}), never as a request body, so a strict old response consumer with additionalProperties:false on a locally-hand-copied shape is the only theoretical break, and no such consumer exists in this workspace's own repos (Backend emits, Frontend/SDKs read via generated/loose types). The field is purely additive and display-only -- it is not in ExperimentGroupOverview's required list, is not referenced by any identity_state allOf branch (identified/unidentified/absent-legacy), and is not part of the group sort/tie-break vocabulary or any cursor/pagination key.

Tightens status (255 -> 64) and error_message (5000 -> 2000) to match the caps the backend already enforces at POST /api/v1/sessions/{session_id}/results (_validate_optional_string_field(data, "status", max_length=64) and MAX_TRIAL_ERROR_MESSAGE_LENGTH = 2_000 in src/services/traigent/terminal_outcome.py, both in TraigentBackend and both pre-existing, unrelated to this schema change). Before this fix the schema was looser than the backend for these two fields, the same too-loose-vs-backend bug class this PR (#454) fixed for the three new fields (summary_stats/execution_mode/execution_environment) on the same endpoint: a client validating a >64-char status or a >2000-char error_message against the schema saw it pass, then the live backend rejected it with 400 -- a false green on a submission the API would never accept. Tightening closes that gap instead of leaving it silently un-ported alongside the widening this PR already makes.

selection is a new OPTIONAL member of the closed SessionAggregationDTO (R3 selection receipt: records the SDK's selection decision and binds it to the session's own trials). The gate flags it under the bare-named-resource conservative heuristic because the old shape was additionalProperties:false and is echoed back in the finalize response. The Backend only echoes session_aggregation it persisted from the SDK's own finalize request, and no producer emits selection yet (Backend normalizer is R3 PR 2, Python SDK producer is PR 3), so a current SDK strictly validating the echo never receives the member; the SDK upgrade that sends selection ships together with the reader. Unreleased. Acknowledged rather than silenced so the widening of a closed shape is visible in the contract history.

NormalizationStrategy was narrowed to ["min_max"] in #217 while z_score/robust were advertised but unimplemented (fail-closed contract half of a bug fix; the SDK made them raise NotImplementedError). Traigent/traigent-smartopt now implements deterministic z_score and robust normalization math with explicit handling for zero-span/zero-scale populations, single-sample populations, and non-finite values, so the prior fail-closed reason no longer holds and the contract is re-widened deliberately. This is additive-only: existing min_max payloads are unaffected, and the only behavior change is that two previously-rejected enum values now validate. tests/test_session_create_objectives_schema.py::test_session_create_accepts_z_score_and_robust_normalization is the differential proof (red against origin/develop's narrow enum, green after this widening).

The experiment resource's status was mis-bound to ExperimentRunStatus (the 9-member run-level vocabulary) while the Backend backs the experiment resource with a distinct 8-member ExperimentStatus enum (TraigentSchema#262). This is a contract-breaking narrowing of a REQUEST field: PAUSED and PARTIALLY_DELETED were schema-valid and are now rejected; REGISTERED was schema-invalid and is now accepted. Observed at TraigentBackend origin/develop 56e66ca824fa: the experiment persistence enum `src/models/status_enums.py:97` has exactly the 8 members {NOT_STARTED, PENDING, REGISTERED, RUNNING, FAILED, COMPLETED, CANCELLED, UNKNOWN}; `POST /api/v1/experiments` with status PAUSED or PARTIALLY_DELETED returns HTTP 422 ("is not a valid ExperimentStatus") and with REGISTERED returns 201 (integration probe against the Flask test app); the list filter rejects non-members with 400 (`src/routes/experiment_routes.py:605-612`). `derive_reported_experiment_status` passes unrecognised stored strings through, so it is not cited as an enum bound. So the narrowed request values are ones the Backend already refuses; whether any client sends them is not claimed.

Same mis-binding fix as the create-request entry above (TraigentSchema#262): the experiment resource's top-level status is rebound from the run-level ExperimentRunStatus to the newly-minted, distinct 8-member ExperimentStatus enum matching the backend's experiment-level persistence enum (`src/models/status_enums.py:97`). PAUSED/PARTIALLY_DELETED are not members of the Backend's experiment persistence enum (see the create-request entry for the pinned evidence); REGISTERED is a real experiment-level state the schema previously could not express at all. Scoped only to this bare-named resource's top-level status -- the embedded ExperimentListRunSummary.status (the latest run's own status) is unchanged and correctly stays on ExperimentRunStatus.

The metric-name character class is being WIDENED from ^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$ to ^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_.-]*$ so that real metric names carrying a hyphen or a dot ("response-time", "cost.usd") are expressible. The new class is a strict superset of the old one: same anchors, same first-character class, and the trailing class only gains '.' and '-'. Every name that validated before this change still validates after it, so no payload that was accepted becomes rejected. This is proved exhaustively, not asserted, by tests/test_metric_name_pattern_consistency.py::test_widened_pattern_is_a_strict_superset_of_the_old_one, which enumerates every string up to length 3 over a boundary-spanning alphabet and fails if any name accepted by the old pattern is rejected by the new one. Context: issue #304 -- sessions and experiments accepted different objective representations, and the legacy {metric,direction,weight} form allowed any 1-255 character string where the canonical form required a Python identifier. Collapsing to the single canonical form (owner decision 2026-09-18) would therefore have silently dropped any objective whose metric name contained a hyphen or dot. Widening is the precondition for that migration, not an independent loosening. TVAR and agent names in optimization/tvar_definition_schema.json are deliberately NOT widened -- they become Python keyword arguments in user code -- and a consistency test pins that split in both directions. This entry covers the paired 'patternProperties key added' finding, which is the other half of the same in-place rewrite.

entries.reason: AccuracyEvaluation.ci_method was a const pinned to clt_mean_standard_error (mean +/- z*SE of the mean over per-example scores); the CLT interval collapses to zero width when every per-example score is identical, which is exactly what happens for binary (0/1) per-example accuracy scoring. The Backend now uses a 95% Wilson score interval on k/n instead when every per-example score is exactly 0 or 1, and keeps CLT for fractional scores (a zero-variance fractional sample still fails closed to CANNOT_DETERMINE, unchanged). Widening the const to a closed two-member enum lets the Backend publish the method it actually used instead of a false clt_mean_standard_error label on binary samples; both methods are Backend-computed and never client-supplied, so this is additive and reviewed, not a silent loosening. Fixture cases added: a valid DeclaredAccuracyTarget evaluation using wilson_score_binary, and a rejected unknown ci_method string.

TraigentSchema#573. x_extensions_meta_schema.json is the annotation vocabulary for x-* keywords, not a wire body: nothing serialises it and no request or response is validated against it, so the conservative bare-resource-name rule applies both request- and response-breaking rule sets to a document neither side ever sends. The widening also removes no accepted value. x-reference was declared "type": "string" (a $ref-style pointer) while 80 of its 109 shipped sites carry the boolean true, meaning "references a canonical identifier, target not yet pinned"; 29 carry the pointer. The declaration, not the usage, was wrong, and #573 made that visible by adding the first test that validates x-* VALUES against this meta-schema. Widening to oneOf [string, const true] makes the declaration describe what ships; tightening it the other way would mean rewriting 80 sites with pointers nobody has chosen yet. The boolean branch is a ratchet, not a second blessed form: tests/data/x_reference_boolean_baseline.txt freezes the 80 sites by file and JSON pointer, and tests/test_x_extensions_governance.py::test_boolean_x_reference_sites_match_the_frozen_baseline fails on any site added AND on any removed without its baseline line being deleted. A per-site inventory rather than a count, because a count reports no change when one site is deleted and another added, and names no file when it does fire. One alternative was weighed and rejected: keep "type": "string" and exempt the 80 sites in the test instead, which would need no acknowledgement here. It was rejected because it leaves the PUBLISHED meta-schema stating a rule that 73% of its own shipped uses break, moving the contradiction out of the contract and into a test where consumers cannot see it; this package's schemas are the product, and the test is not. Rewriting the 80 sites with real pointers was also rejected: the targets have not been chosen, and inventing them would be fabricated data that no test resolves. Scoped to this one pointer.

TraigentSchema#591 review. The declared 200 for this route matched NO real response and therefore cannot have a working consumer to break. The analytics blueprint handler returns response_handler.success_response(...), so the wire body is {success, message, data} with the dashboard payload under data; the entry declared the bare payload, which requires its five fields at the ROOT with additionalProperties:false. Every successful call failed that schema. The repository's own authoritative record agrees: success_envelope_schema.json's x-wrap-map lists analytics_routes under `wrapped`, not `bare`, and the route is not among the per-operation exceptions in x-wrap-map.mixed. The findings below are the artefacts of moving the declaration from the payload to the envelope that contains it: additionalProperties opens because the canonical envelope is open, `data` appears, and the five payload fields stop being root-level requirements because they are now required one level down, inside data, by the SAME unchanged payload schema (projects/project_scoped_optimization_overview_dashboard_schema.json is not touched). Nothing is loosened in substance: a body that satisfies the new declaration contains exactly the same required payload. No cross-repo coordination is needed for THIS change because its direction is forced, not chosen: making the server return a bare body instead would contradict the repo's own wrap-map and the convention of twelve route files, so there is no second option to coordinate. (The separate residual in TraigentSchema#594 - summary_cards.experiments_in_range is required and emitted by nobody - is deliberately NOT fixed here precisely because its direction IS a choice: either the schema drops the field or the backend emits it, and nothing on record picks one. So this change narrows the contract-vs-wire gap to one field; it does not close it.) One handler serves this v1beta mount and the unscoped /api/v1 mount, so fixing one and leaving the other would have left the two declarations of a single handler disagreeing. Scoped to this one route's 200.

entries.reason: The extensions meta-schema is the registry of allowed x-* annotation keywords, not a wire payload: no request or response body is validated against it, so declaring the two new annotations x-write-only and x-requires-project-binding (used on the fleet_imports:write scope map entry) cannot make any consumer reject a payload. The registry is closed by design, so each new annotation must be added here.

The 400 on GET /api/v1/analytics/dashboards/optimization-overview documented a status the backend never returns for this operation: query validation is ProjectOptimizationOverviewDashboardQuery through response_handler.validation_error_response, which pins HTTP 422 with error_code VALIDATION_ERROR (TraigentBackend src/utils/response_handler.py validation_error_response; handler src/routes/analytics_routes.py get_project_optimization_overview_dashboard). The 422 is now declared in its place, so a client written to the old 400 would never have seen it fire. No malformed request changed behaviour; only the declaration was wrong.

The 401/403/404/500 responses of GET /api/v1/analytics/dashboards/optimization-overview keep a body schema: they moved into shared #/components/responses entries (AnalyticsUnauthenticated, AnalyticsForbidden, AnalyticsProjectNotFound, AnalyticsInternalError) that all 33 analytics operations share, and the checker does not follow response $refs, so it reads the move as removal. The 401, 403 and 500 bodies are unchanged (error_envelope_schema.json). The 404 body is unchanged in shape: it stays the ordinary application/json error envelope (error_envelope_schema.json), now shared as AnalyticsProjectNotFound; a project that does not exist, or in which the caller holds no role, returns 404 PROJECT_NOT_FOUND through project-context resolution (TraigentBackend src/security/project_context.py, caught by unified_auth in src/security/unified_auth.py:2072-2073, rendered via src/security/unified_auth.py:1980-1985 and error_response in src/utils/response_handler.py:332-378). No application/problem+json 404 is declared because the analytics mounts carry no project-entry guards (src/routes/api_v1beta.py:117, src/api_kit/mounts.py:247). AnalyticsResourceNotFound additionally covers the handler not_found_response branches (missing experiment, measure or export job); this overview has no such branch.

The eleven project analytics path keys in planned_projects_endpoints.json are not removed from the contract: each keeps its path key and now carries a path-item $ref to the canonical declaration in analytics/analytics_endpoints.json (the backend master catalog loads that file), where it is declared once with its backend operation id project_analytics.<suffix>, the same method and the same path. The checker reads the planned catalog without following path-item $refs, so it reports the move as removal; the same operations appear as endpoint_added in analytics/analytics_endpoints.json for all three mounts. SchemaValidator resolves the path-item $ref, so contract=planned_projects still knows all eleven (tests/test_validator.py, tests/test_planned_projects_endpoint_paths.py). The operationIds change from camel-case ids (getProjectAnalyticsSummary and ten siblings) to the backend ids; the Python SDK, JS SDK and portal pins checked for the plan do not dispatch through them.

The fine-tuning manifest response gains the two members the backend always emits, truncated (boolean) and empty_reason (null or the one closed reason string), at core_domain_analytics_service.export_fine_tuning_manifest (the return dict, 'truncated' and 'empty_reason'). The schema is closed (additionalProperties false) and omitted them, so a strict validator already rejected every real manifest; declaring them makes real responses valid. Response-only: no request body changes, and a producer that emits the backend's actual payload is unaffected.

truncated and empty_reason are added to the required list of the fine-tuning manifest response because the backend emits both on every successful export (core_domain_analytics_service.export_fine_tuning_manifest always sets 'truncated' and 'empty_reason', including empty and failed-to-record-job cases). Response-only requirement matching the real payload; it cannot reject any response the backend produces. A third-party producer or mock that omits them would now fail validation, which is the intended tightening: the old schema rejected the real payload, the new one accepts it.

The agent readiness detail response gains the optional, nullable top-level scorecard (scores and per-area stats against the latest active config, or the current run when none is promoted). The response is additionalProperties:false, so a strict reader built from the previous schema rejects a body carrying it. Rollout rule: strict readers of the detail response must upgrade to this schema before the Backend starts emitting scorecard; the Backend change ships with this contract. Payloads without the field still validate.

Backend API revision W9 moves the experiment-group reads to project-scoped paths and removes the old ones: GET /api/v1/experiment-groups becomes POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/experiment-groups/search (experiment_group.list_groups; cursor-only, filters and search text in the body); GET /api/v1/experiment-groups/{group_id} becomes GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/experiment-groups/{group_ref} (experiment_group.get_group); GET /api/v1/experiment-groups/{group_id}/configuration-runs becomes GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/experiment-groups/{group_ref}/configuration-runs (experiment_group.list_group_runs); POST /api/v1/experiment-groups/{group_id}/configuration-runs/query becomes POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/experiment-groups/{group_ref}/configuration-runs/query (experiment_group.query_group_runs). The group detail no longer embeds source_experiments: they are paged by the new GET .../{group_ref}/experiments (experiment_group.list_group_experiments). page, per_page and offset are gone (cursor and limit only) and errors are closed application/problem+json bodies. Consumers: the Traigent portal (updated in the same release) and the Python SDK (traigent 0.34). The shapes match the backend implementation of API revision W9.

Unreleased pre-release path move: the 14 production reactive operations in optimization/tvl_reactive_endpoints.json move from /api/v1/production-reactive/agents/{agent_ref}/... to /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/agents/{agent_ref}/production-reactive/... and gain the project_id path parameter. operationIds, methods, bodies and responses are unchanged.
